issues.competing_evidence: Stark+08 calls 1RXS J165630.2-083442 the likely optical counterpart; exact RASS-BSC separation ~9.7 arcsec with 10 arcsec position error. 2RXS is ~8.2 arcsec from Gaia. Pointed 1WGA is ~16.7 arcsec away with a 90% 50-arcsec radius; SIMBAD does not list the WGA alias.
issues.why_it_matters: Association affects X-ray luminosity and radio/X-ray comparison.
issues.needed_action: Retain as probable; confirm with higher-resolution X-ray data/archive astrometry before calling the ROSAT flux securely matched.

issues.competing_evidence: Stark+08 reports 0.1952894(10) d. Bruch & Diaz+17 reports refined 0.1952913(3) d from 2015 line-phase offsets and baseline-scaled uncertainty. Hewitt+20 repeats Stark. The two measurements differ by 1.9e-6 d (~1.8 sigma from quoted errors).
issues.why_it_matters: The period sets long-term phase predictions and errors are method dependent.
issues.needed_action: For phase-sensitive use, review retaining Bruch & Diaz as compatibility value; keep both values and uncertainty methods.

issues.competing_evidence: Stark+08 DIB 5780 gives E(B−V)~0.50 if narrow component alone or ~0.24 for narrow+broad (authors prefer latter); DIB 4430 gives ~0.12. Schlegel full-column is ~0.47 and not source-specific. IX Vel color comparison suggests ~0.10; authors deem 0.10–0.20 plausible.
issues.why_it_matters: Extinction shifts CMD color and absolute magnitude; arbitrary selection would bias intrinsic comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep observed Gaia CMD values. If intrinsic CMD needed, determine source-specific reddening from updated 3D dust or spectroscopy; preserve published branches.

issues.competing_evidence: Bruch & Diaz+17 arbitrary overlay uses i=60°, M2=.43 Msun, q=.52 from M1=.83 in prose, but Fig. 5 caption says M1=.75. Hewitt+20 SED inputs M1=.75, M2=.45 Msun, i=57°, Mdot=5e-9 Msun/yr are explicitly unknown/estimated. None are source-specific measurements.
issues.references: Bruch+Diaz+17_LSIV-08-3; Hewitt+20; Knigge+11 as cited by Bruch
issues.why_it_matters: Mislabeling assumptions as measurements would bias component comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep out of measured-value fields. Decide only whether future public display needs a separate model-assumptions section.

issues.competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 3 reports <33 uJy; §4.2 notes and rejects a roughly 3-sigma feature about 6 arcsec from optical position.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating the feature as detection changes the radio status and population comparison.
issues.needed_action: Retain upper limit; verify astrometry from raw images if available before representing as a candidate.

issues.competing_evidence: SIMBAD object type is CV*, but its sp_type field says sdB. Stark+08 documents earlier OB/hot-subdwarf classification and reclassifies as UX UMa CV; the SIMBAD label appears legacy rather than a component spectrum.
issues.why_it_matters: Using stale sdB metadata as a WD/donor type would misidentify physical components.
issues.needed_action: Retain as historical/conflicting metadata only; any public type must include source/date and not assign sdB to a component.

references.note: arXiv record inspected. AJ paper "A New, Bright, Short-Period, Emission Line Binary in Ophiuchus". Abstract verifies LS IV -08 3 was previously catalogued as OB/hot subdwarf but is a binary UX UMa-type CV; H-alpha radial velocities give Porb=0.1952894(10) d; high-resolution spectra show broad and narrow anti-phased emission components plausibly from disk and irradiated donor; photometry shows low-amplitude orbital-timescale variability; DIB reddening is consistent with distance ~100-200 pc; weak ROSAT counterpart properties match accretion in a CV. Full PDF not downloaded locally in this pass. Corrected inherited DOI: 10.1086/586730 belongs to an unrelated article; verified DOI is 10.1088/0004-6256/135/3/991. Full AJ paper and tables checked locally.
